title: Comparison Operators
objectives: Work out the TRUE/FALSE result of a comparison expression

hook.text: The expression "age ≥ 18" is not a number, it is a QUESTION. Its answer is either TRUE or FALSE.

concept.heading: Six comparison operators
concept.body: = is equal to, ≠ is not equal to, < is less than, > is greater than, ≤ is less than or equal to, ≥ is greater than or equal to. The result of these operators is always a boolean value (TRUE/FALSE), never a numeric value.

concept.heading: Why does it matter?
concept.body: Comparisons are the foundation of the IF command you will learn in the next lesson. The expression "IF age ≥ 18" first works out the comparison age ≥ 18 as TRUE or FALSE, then picks a branch based on that result.

workedExamples.prompt: When age ← 20, what is the result of the expression "age ≥ 18"?

steps.explain: 20 is put into the age box.
The comparison 20 ≥ 18 gives the result TRUE.
TRUE is written to the screen.

exercises.question: What is the result of the expression "5 ≠ 5"?

feedback.correct: Correct. 5 is equal to 5, so the "not equal" expression is FALSE.
feedback.incorrect: 5 and 5 are equal, so the "≠" (not equal) expression gives FALSE.
